skill.name: hyperframes-core
skill.description: Guides creation and review of HyperFrames HTML video compositions, including structure, timing attributes, clips, tracks, sub-compositions, variables, media, Tailwind, and validation.
skill.summary: Build renderable HyperFrames video compositions with deterministic timing, tracks, variables, sub-compositions, and validation guidance.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown inline code, HTML examples, Tailwind template literals, and HyperFrames naming rules. The CDN script examples and npx validation commands are real low-to-medium operational risks. The headless CLI worker fallback is a higher-risk semantic issue.

remediation.issue: Remote CDN runtime dependency in composition examples
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a bundled or locally vendored GSAP runtime, or clearly document that rendering may fetch a third-party script.

remediation.issue: npx HyperFrames commands execute external package code
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running CLI validation, preview, snapshot, or render commands, and pin the package source when possible.

remediation.issue: Headless CLI worker fallback can bypass delegation controls
remediation.suggestion: Remove the fallback that launches background CLI workers without a delegation grant, or require explicit user approval for that shell-based path.

semantic_findings.title: Headless CLI Worker Fallback Can Bypass Delegation Controls
semantic_findings.description: The subagent dispatch guide says Codex spawning needs explicit user delegation, then recommends headless CLI children when no grant is present. Launching background CLI workers through the shell can bypass the intended delegation policy boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The relevant lines directly describe the policy gate and the fallback to background shell-driven CLI workers. This is a documented workflow risk, not inferred from a weak token match.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects can fail from small timing, layout, media, or sub-composition mistakes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a precise composition contract.
actual_capabilities: Guides standalone and sub-composition project structure for HyperFrames HTML videos.
Documents required data attributes for roots, clips, tracks, variables, and media.
Explains deterministic timeline rules for seekable rendering and repeatable frames.
Provides Tailwind v4 guidance for browser-runtime video compositions.
Defines storyboard and script planning formats for video production workflows.
Maps validation steps to HyperFrames lint, validate, inspect, snapshot, preview, and render checks.
limitations: Does not provide detailed animation runtime APIs for GSAP, Lottie, or Three.js.
Does not generate or license media assets for a video project.
Requires HyperFrames tooling to validate, preview, snapshot, or render outputs.
Some documented workflows use network dependencies or CLI commands that need review.

use_cases.title: Build a Renderable Composition
use_cases.description: Create a fixed-size HyperFrames HTML project with root attributes, clips, tracks, variables, media, and a paused timeline.

use_cases.title: Modularize Scene-Based Videos
use_cases.description: Split a multi-scene video into a thin orchestrator and sub-composition files with matching IDs and deterministic timing.

use_cases.title: Validate Tailwind Video Layouts
use_cases.description: Review Tailwind v4 composition markup for static class safety, fixed dimensions, media placement, and render-safe animation rules.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single-scene video.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-core to create a minimal standalone HyperFrames composition for a 1920 by 1080, five-second intro. Include the required root attributes, one clip, and a paused timeline.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Scene Timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this storyboard and propose HyperFrames clips, track indexes, durations, and variables before writing HTML. Keep the plan deterministic.

prompt_templates.title: Convert to Sub-Compositions
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this monolithic HyperFrames project into a modular orchestrator with one file per scene. Preserve IDs, timing, media paths, and variables.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Render Determinism
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before preview or render.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this HyperFrames project for render-determinism issues, Tailwind v4 risks, sub-composition wiring, media placement, and validation steps.

output_examples.output: A minimal composition plan with fixed dimensions, one root clip, a paused timeline, media placement guidance, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Refactor three inline scenes into modular files.
output_examples.output: A modular layout with an index orchestrator, three scene files, matching composition IDs, preserved timing, and a render checklist.

output_examples.input: Check whether this Tailwind composition is render-safe.
output_examples.output: A review summary that flags dynamic classes, breakpoint variants, unstable sizing, and media placement issues with practical replacements.

best_practices: Read the targeted reference file before editing composition HTML.
Keep timelines seekable and avoid clocks, unseeded randomness, and render-time network state.
Confirm project context and user approval before running HyperFrames CLI commands.
anti_patterns: Mixing monolithic and modular scene patterns in one project.
Using dynamic Tailwind class names for render-critical styles.
Placing audio or video inside a sub-composition template.

faq.question: Is this skill for writing HyperFrames HTML?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the composition contract for roots, clips, tracks, variables, media, and deterministic timelines.

faq.question: Does it render the video by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents how to build and validate projects. Rendering requires HyperFrames tooling.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Tailwind v4 runtime rules, static class safety, fixed dimensions, and validation checks.

faq.question: Does it include animation API details?
faq.answer: Only the core contract. Runtime-specific APIs are delegated to the companion animation skill.

faq.question: Can it work with sub-compositions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains host slots, templates, matching composition IDs, variables, and per-scene validation.

faq.question: What should users review before running commands?
faq.answer: Review the workspace, command intent, package source, and any network dependency before running CLI validation or rendering.
